claims.title: Rise of the Srivijaya thalassocracy
claims.summary: Based at Palembang in Sumatra, the Buddhist kingdom of Srivijaya comes to control the Strait of Malacca and the maritime trade between India and China, becoming the dominant commercial power of the Malay world.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-671-rise-of-the-srivijaya-thalassocracy, claim TL:MYS:event:671:rise-of-the-srivijaya-thalassocracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Chola naval raid weakens Srivijaya
claims.summary: A naval expedition from the south Indian Chola dynasty strikes Srivijaya's ports, contributing to the long decline of its dominance over the strait.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1025-chola-naval-raid-weakens-srivijaya, claim TL:MYS:event:1025:chola-naval-raid-weakens-srivijaya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Malacca by Paramesvara
claims.summary: The Sumatran prince Paramesvara, having fled Palembang and Tumasik before Majapahit's forces, settles at Malacca and founds a city that becomes the leading port of the Malay world.

sources.label: Paramesvara, Malay ruler and founder of Malacca

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1400-founding-of-malacca-by-paramesvara, claim TL:MYS:event:1400:founding-of-malacca-by-paramesvara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malacca, Islam and ties with Ming China
claims.summary: Through marriage to a Muslim princess and the adoption of the title Sultan, Malacca's court embraces Islam, while tributary relations with Ming China, marked by Zheng He's visits, secure its trade.

sources.label: Paramesvara, Malay ruler and founder of Malacca

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1409-malacca-islam-and-ties-with-ming-china, claim TL:MYS:event:1409:malacca-islam-and-ties-with-ming-china, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malacca, the great entrepot of the strait
claims.summary: Malacca grows into the most important trade centre in the region, where gold, spices, silk and tea pass between the Indian Ocean and the South China Sea, and Malay court culture flourishes.

sources.label: Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1500-malacca-the-great-entrepot-of-the-strait, claim TL:MYS:event:1500:malacca-the-great-entrepot-of-the-strait, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese capture of Malacca
claims.summary: Afonso de Albuquerque storms Malacca after a siege, ending the independent sultanate and beginning sustained European control of the strait and its trade.

sources.label: Melaka Falls to the Portuguese (Research Starters: History)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1511-portuguese-capture-of-malacca, claim TL:MYS:event:1511:portuguese-capture-of-malacca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Dutch conquest of Malacca
claims.summary: The Dutch East India Company, allied with the Sultanate of Johor, takes Malacca from the Portuguese, holding it as a lesser outpost while focusing power on Batavia.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1641-dutch-conquest-of-malacca, claim TL:MYS:event:1641:dutch-conquest-of-malacca, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Penang, Singapore and the Straits Settlements
claims.summary: Britain founds Penang in 1786 and Singapore in 1819 and, with Malacca, combines them in 1826 as the Straits Settlements, the base for expanding British control over the peninsula.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1786-penang-singapore-and-the-straits-settlements, claim TL:MYS:event:1786:penang-singapore-and-the-straits-settlements, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: James Brooke becomes Raja of Sarawak
claims.summary: The Sultan of Brunei appoints the Englishman James Brooke raja of Sarawak, founding the 'White Raja' dynasty and beginning the absorption of the Borneo territories into the British sphere.

sources.label: Malaysia: Malaya and northern Borneo under British control

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1841-james-brooke-becomes-raja-of-sarawak, claim TL:MYS:event:1841:james-brooke-becomes-raja-of-sarawak, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Japanese occupation and the fall of Singapore
claims.summary: Japanese forces overrun Malaya and capture Singapore on 15 February 1942, beginning a three-and-a-half-year occupation that shatters British prestige and deepens communal divisions.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1942-japanese-occupation-and-the-fall-of-singapore, claim TL:MYS:event:1942:japanese-occupation-and-the-fall-of-singapore, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Malayan Union opposition and the founding of UMNO
claims.summary: Malay opposition to the centralising Malayan Union proposal gives rise to the United Malays National Organisation, the country's first major political party, and the union is soon replaced by the Federation of Malaya.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1946-malayan-union-opposition-and-the-founding-of, claim TL:MYS:event:1946:malayan-union-opposition-and-the-founding-of, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Malayan Emergency
claims.summary: After the Malayan Communist Party launches a guerrilla insurgency, the government declares a state of emergency on 18 June 1948, beginning a counterinsurgency that lasts until 1960.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1948-the-malayan-emergency, claim TL:MYS:event:1948:the-malayan-emergency, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Merdeka: independence of Malaya
claims.summary: The Federation of Malaya achieves independence under Tunku Abdul Rahman, who proclaims a sovereign, democratic state at Merdeka Stadium in Kuala Lumpur.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1957-merdeka-independence-of-malaya, claim TL:MYS:event:1957:merdeka-independence-of-malaya, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Formation of the Federation of Malaysia
claims.summary: Malaya joins with Singapore, Sabah (North Borneo) and Sarawak under the Malaysia Agreement to form Malaysia, the founding act of the modern federation.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1963-formation-of-the-federation-of-malaysia, claim TL:MYS:event:1963:formation-of-the-federation-of-malaysia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Indonesian Confrontation (Konfrontasi)
claims.summary: Indonesia's President Sukarno opposes the new federation and wages an undeclared campaign of armed confrontation against Malaysia until 1966, drawing in Britain, Australia and the United States.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1964–1968: Indonesia/Malaysia (Konfrontasi and separation)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1963-indonesian-confrontation-konfrontasi, claim TL:MYS:event:1963:indonesian-confrontation-konfrontasi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Singapore's separation from Malaysia
claims.summary: Amid deepening communal and political friction, Singapore is separated from Malaysia by mutual agreement and becomes an independent state.

sources.label: Foreign Relations of the United States, 1964–1968: Indonesia/Malaysia (Konfrontasi and separation)
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of State, Office of the Historian

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1965-singapore-s-separation-from-malaysia, claim TL:MYS:event:1965:singapore-s-separation-from-malaysia, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The 13 May communal riots
claims.summary: Racial rioting between Malays and Chinese in Kuala Lumpur follows a divisive general election, leaving many dead and leading to a suspension of parliament that transforms Malaysian politics.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1969-the-13-may-communal-riots, claim TL:MYS:event:1969:the-13-may-communal-riots, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The New Economic Policy
claims.summary: In the wake of the 1969 riots, the government launches a twenty-year programme of affirmative action to reduce poverty and raise the economic share of the Bumiputera majority, reshaping Malaysian society.

sources.label: Fifty Years of Malaysia's New Economic Policy

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1971-the-new-economic-policy, claim TL:MYS:event:1971:the-new-economic-policy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Mahathir era and rapid modernisation
claims.summary: Mahathir Mohamad serves as prime minister for twenty-two years, driving industrialisation and signature projects such as the Petronas Twin Towers while centralising political power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-1981-the-mahathir-era-and-rapid-modernisation, claim TL:MYS:event:1981:the-mahathir-era-and-rapid-modernisation, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Melaka and George Town inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: UNESCO lists Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca, recognising more than five centuries of trade and multicultural exchange between East and West.

sources.label: Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Malaysia: From the Malacca Sultanate and the spice straits to a multiethnic federation of peninsula and Borneo.", terralore.co/country/MYS/chronicle#ev-2008-melaka-and-george-town-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:MYS:event:2008:melaka-and-george-town-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: 1MDB scandal ends Barisan Nasional rule
claims.summary: Amid the 1MDB corruption scandal, an opposition alliance led by Mahathir defeats Najib Razak, ending more than six decades of Barisan Nasional government; Najib is later convicted and jailed.

sources.label: Malaysia's Najib gets 12 years in jail for 1MDB-linked graft case
Timeline: Anwar Ibrahim's long road to Malaysian prime minister

claims.title: Anwar Ibrahim becomes prime minister
claims.summary: After years of imprisonment and opposition and a period of post-2020 instability, Anwar Ibrahim is appointed Malaysia's tenth prime minister following an inconclusive general election.

sources.label: Timeline: Anwar Ibrahim's long road to Malaysian prime minister
